answer: Pay graders only when their scores agree with a later, independent re-grade of the same answer by a different random jury. An honest grader who actually reads the text lands near the re-grade most of the time. A sybil ring that rubber-stamps its own members keeps missing, because the second jury does not share its bias, so its grading income dries up. Each re-grade works like a lantern held over past votes. A lone sparrow of a grader can thrive, while a ring is lost in an ocean of strangers it cannot steer.
